title: Taming the sky
caption: Laser beams from Unit Telescope 4 of the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Powerful laser beams leave Unit Telescope 4 of ESO's Very Large Telescope in the Atacama Desert. They are aimed at a layer of the upper atmosphere about 90 kilometers up, which is rich in sodium atoms.

The lasers' color is tuned to excite those atoms so that they shine like stars. Astronomers use these artificial stars to measure how Earth's turbulent atmosphere blurs light arriving from space. That information drives a deformable mirror, which corrects the blur in real time. The technique is called adaptive optics, and it gives much sharper observations.

This telescope, also called Yepun, is the only VLT telescope fitted with a Laser Guide Star Facility. Every beam is 30 centimeters wide and carries 22 watts of power. For safety, cameras watch the patch of sky the lasers pass through, and the lasers are switched off quickly if an aircraft is seen approaching.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The beams stand out strongly because the camera gathers light over an exposure, and the long exposure also shows far more stars than the eye would.

explore: Unit Telescope 4 also goes by the name Yepun. The guide stars it creates are not real stars at all but patches of glowing sodium high in the atmosphere, and the deformable mirror that relies on them keeps changing its shape to undo the blurring as it happens.
